title: analysis.table.summarize request
description: Summarize a fixed-layout table's columns — distinct values, their frequencies, and the numeric extremes — and compare those columns across several sources read with the same layout. Every count is exact and every list is capped, so a capped list never reads as the whole set. `read_only`: accepts only the `read` execution mode.

oneOf.description: The record spelled out in the request.
The record named: a struct the project defines. Needs the envelope's `project` locator.

sources.description: The tables to summarize, each read with the same layout at the same offset. Naming several is the point: comparing one column across the memory several sandbox runs exported is the question this exists for. The order is part of the question — a comparison reports one value per table by position.

layout.description: Comma-separated field list, e.g. `u16,u16,ptr,char[16]`. Scalars are `u8`/`u16`/`u32` and their signed forms, `ptr` is a 32-bit pointer, `char[N]` a NUL-terminated Latin-1 string, `bytes[N]` raw bytes, and `pad[N]` skipped bytes.

type_id.description: A `type:` id naming a struct the project defines, used instead of `layout`. The struct's fields are read back as a record layout, so a table saved as a resource decodes from the stored type alone — which is what `type_id` on a table resource has always meant and nothing could act on. The struct must describe a contiguous run of fields a layout can express: a gap, an overlap, a declared size its fields do not reach, or a field of a type no layout has is refused rather than decoded as something else.

offset.description: Byte offset of the first record.

rows.description: How many records to read from each source. A region that holds fewer whole rows contributes the ones that fit and reports its true count.

maximum_values.description: Cap on the distinct values listed per column. `distinct_total` beside the list is always exact.

maximum_differences.description: Cap on the rows listed per column where the sources disagree. `differing_total` beside the list is always exact.
